event-title.$: ENTRY INTO FORCE OF REQUEST FOR SUBSTANTIVE EXAMINATION

section.content: When a vehicle component is replaced, the estimation accuracy of a machine learning model used in the vehicle is lowered. The machine learning device is provided with: a learning unit (31) that performs learning of a machine learning model used in the vehicle (1); and a detection unit (32) that detects replacement of a vehicle component mounted on the vehicle. When a vehicle component related to input data of a machine learning model is replaced, a learning unit performs relearning of the machine learning model using a training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component.
在车辆部件被进行了更换的情况下，在车辆中使用的机器学习模型的推定精度会降低。机器学习装置具备：学习部(31)，其进行在车辆(1)中使用的机器学习模型的学习；和检测部(32)，其对搭载于车辆的车辆部件的更换进行检测。学习部在与机器学习模型的输入数据有关的车辆部件被进行了更换的情况下，使用与更换后的车辆部件对应的训练数据集，进行机器学习模型的再学习。

Machine learning deviceTechnical Field

The present invention relates to a machine learning device.

Background

In recent years, with the advancement of AI (artificial intelligence) technology, control using a machine learning model such as a neural network model in a vehicle has been studied. For example, in the machine learning system described in patent document 1, the temperature of an exhaust gas purification catalyst provided in an internal combustion engine is estimated using a neural network model.

In order to improve the estimation accuracy of such a neural network model, it is necessary to learn the neural network model in advance. For example, as described in patent document 1, learning of the neural network model is performed in a server, and the learned neural network model is transmitted from the server to the vehicle.

Prior art literature

Patent document 1: japanese patent laid-open No. 2019-183698

Disclosure of Invention

Technical problem to be solved by the invention

When deterioration or malfunction of a vehicle component occurs with use of the vehicle, replacement of the vehicle component is performed. In addition, in some cases, replacement of vehicle components is performed in order to mount higher-performance vehicle components on the vehicle.

However, machine learning models used in vehicles are often matched to the characteristics of the vehicle components prior to replacement. Therefore, when the characteristics of the vehicle component become abnormal due to the replacement of the vehicle component, there is a risk that the estimation accuracy of the machine learning model is lowered.

In view of the above, an object of the present invention is to suppress a decrease in estimation accuracy of a machine learning model used in a vehicle when a vehicle component is replaced.

Technical scheme for solving problems

The gist of the present disclosure is as follows.

(1) A machine learning device is provided with: a learning unit that learns a machine learning model used in a vehicle; and a detection unit that detects replacement of a vehicle component mounted on the vehicle, wherein the learning unit performs relearning of the machine learning model using a training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component when the vehicle component related to the input data of the machine learning model is replaced.

(2) The machine learning device according to the above (1), wherein the learning unit performs the relearning of the machine learning model by using the training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component only when the vehicle component related to the input data of the machine learning model is replaced with a vehicle component having a different structure.

(3) The machine learning device according to the above (1) or (2), further comprising an updating unit that updates the machine learning model, wherein the learning unit is provided in a server and transmits a relearned machine learning model to the vehicle, and wherein the updating unit applies the relearned machine learning model to the vehicle.

(4) The machine learning device according to the above (1) or (2), wherein the learning unit is provided in the vehicle, and applies the relearned machine learning model to the vehicle.

(5) The machine learning device according to any one of the above (1) to (4), wherein the machine learning model is a neural network model, and the learning unit performs relearning of the machine learning model by updating parameters of the machine learning model set before relearning.

ADVANTAGEOUS EFFECTS OF INVENTION

According to the present invention, when a vehicle component is replaced, it is possible to suppress a decrease in estimation accuracy of a machine learning model used in a vehicle.

Detailed Description

Hereinafter, embodiments of the present invention will be described in detail with reference to the accompanying drawings. In the following description, the same reference numerals are given to the same constituent elements.

< First embodiment >, first embodiment

First, a first embodiment of the present invention will be described with reference to fig. 1 to 4. Fig. 1 is a diagram schematically showing a configuration of a vehicle 1 provided with a machine learning device according to a first embodiment of the present invention.

As shown in fig. 1, the vehicle 1 includes an actuator 11, a sensor 12, and an electronic control unit (ECU (Electronic Control Unit, electronic control unit)) 20. That is, the actuator 11, the sensor 12, and the ECU20 are mounted on the vehicle 1. The actuator 11 and the sensor 12 are communicably connected to the ECU20 via an in-vehicle network compliant with a standard such as CAN (Controller Area Network ).

The actuator 11 is a working member required for running of the vehicle 1, and includes, for example, a member required for operation of an internal combustion engine (a spark plug, a fuel injection valve, a throttle valve drive actuator, an EGR control valve, etc.), a motor, a clutch, etc. The ECU20 controls the actuator 11.

The sensor 12 detects state quantities of the vehicle 1, the internal combustion engine, the battery, and the like, including a vehicle speed sensor, a GPS receiver, an accelerator opening sensor, an air flow meter, an air-fuel ratio sensor, a crank angle sensor, a torque sensor, a voltage sensor, a temperature sensor, and the like. The output of the sensor 12 is sent to the ECU20.

The actuator 11 and the sensor 12 constitute a vehicle component that is a component mounted on the vehicle 1. In other words, the vehicle component includes the actuator 11 and the sensor 12.

The ECU20 includes a communication interface 21, a memory 22, and a processor 23, and executes various controls of the vehicle 1. In the present embodiment, one ECU20 is provided, but a plurality of ECUs may be provided for each function.

The communication interface 21 has an interface circuit for connecting the ECU20 to an in-vehicle network compliant with the CAN or the like standard. The ECU20 communicates with other in-vehicle devices as described above via the communication interface 21.

The memory 22 has, for example, a volatile semiconductor memory (e.g., RAM) and a nonvolatile semiconductor memory (e.g., ROM). The memory 22 stores programs executed in the processor 23, various data used when various processes are executed by the processor 23, and the like.

The processor 23 has one or more CPUs (Central Processing Unit, central processing units) and peripheral circuits thereof, and performs various processes. The processor 23 may further include an arithmetic circuit such as a logic arithmetic unit or a numerical arithmetic unit. The communication interface 21, the memory 22, and the processor 23 are connected to each other via signal lines.

In the present embodiment, the ECU20 functions as a machine learning device. Fig. 2 is a functional block diagram of the ECU20 of fig. 1. The ECU20 has a learning section 31 and a detecting section 32. The learning unit 31 and the detection unit 32 are functional blocks realized by the processor 23 of the ECU20 executing programs stored in the memory 22 of the ECU 20.

The learning unit 31 performs learning of a machine learning model used in the vehicle 1. In the present embodiment, as the machine learning model, a neural network model that outputs at least one output data (also referred to as a destination variable) from a plurality of input data (also referred to as explanatory variables) can be used.

First, an outline of the neural network model will be described with reference to fig. 3. Fig. 3 shows an example of a neural network model having a simple structure.

The circular symbols in fig. 3 represent artificial neurons. Artificial neurons are commonly referred to as nodes or cells (referred to as "nodes" in this specification). In fig. 3, l=1 represents an input layer, l=2 and l=3 represents a hidden layer, and l=4 represents an output layer. Furthermore, the hidden layer is also referred to as an intermediate layer.

In fig. 3, x 1 and x 2 denote each node of the input layer (l=1) and an output value from the node, and y denotes a node of the output layer (l=4) and an output value thereof. Similarly, z 1(L＝2)、z2(L＝2) and z 3(L＝2) denote each node of the hidden layer (l=2) and an output value from the node, and z 1(L＝3) and z 2(L＝3) denote each node of the hidden layer (l=3) and an output value from the node.

At each node of the input layer, the input is directly output. On the other hand, the output values x 1 and x 2 of the nodes of the input layer are input to the nodes of the hidden layer (l=2), and the total input value u is calculated using the weights w and the offsets b corresponding to the nodes of the hidden layer (l=2). For example, in fig. 3, the total input value u k(L＝2) calculated in each node indicated by z k(L＝2) (k=1, 2, 3) of the hidden layer (l=2) is expressed as follows (M is the number of nodes of the input layer).

Then, the total input value u k(L＝2) is converted by the activation function f, and output from the node indicated by z k(L＝2) of the hidden layer (l=2) as an output value z k(L＝2)(＝f(uk(L＝2)). On the other hand, the output values z 1(L＝2)、z2(L＝2) and z 3(L＝2) of the nodes of the hidden layer (l=2) are input to the nodes of the hidden layer (l=3), and the total input value u (=Σz·w+b) is calculated using the weights w and the offsets b corresponding to the nodes of the hidden layer (l=3). The total input value u is similarly converted by an activation function, for example, a Sigmoid function σ, and each node of the hidden layer (l=3) is output as an output value z 1(L＝3)、z2(L＝3).

The output values z 1(L＝3) and z 2(L＝3) of the nodes of the hidden layer (l=3) are input to the node of the output layer (l=4), and the total input value u (Σz·w+b) is calculated using the weights w and the offsets b corresponding to the nodes of the output layer, or the total input value u (Σz·w) is calculated using only the weights w corresponding to the nodes. For example, in a node of the output layer, an identity function is used as the activation function. In this case, the total input value u calculated in the node of the output layer is directly output from the node of the output layer as the output value y.

The neural network model used in the vehicle 1 is stored in the memory 22 of the ECU20 or other storage device provided in the vehicle 1. The ECU20 causes the neural network model to output at least one value (output value) of the output data by inputting values (input values) of a plurality of input data to the neural network model. In this case, as the value of each input data, for example, an output value of the sensor 12, a command value from the ECU20 to the actuator 11, a value calculated in the ECU20, and the like can be used.

The value of the output data output from the neural network model is used for control of the vehicle 1. The neural network model may be any one of a regression model and a classification model. In the case where the neural network model is a regression model, the output data is, for example, the output torque Of the internal combustion engine, the concentration Of a predetermined component (HC, NOx, etc.) in the exhaust gas, the State Of Charge (SOC) Of the battery, or the like. On the other hand, in the case where the neural network model is a classification model, the output data is, for example, a predetermined abnormality determination result of the sensor 12, a start determination result of the internal combustion engine in the hybrid vehicle, or the like. The state quantity associated with the output data is appropriately selected as the input data.

In order to improve the accuracy of such a neural network model, it is necessary to learn the neural network model in advance. Therefore, for example, the neural network model is learned in a production plant of a vehicle or the like.

In learning the neural network model, a training data set composed of a combination of actual measurement values of a plurality of input data and actual measurement values (forward solution data or teacher data) of at least one output data corresponding to the actual measurement values is used. The actual measurement values of the input data and the output data are obtained using, for example, an engine block or the like, and a training data set is created by combining the corresponding actual measurement values.

In learning the neural network model, a large number of training data sets are used, and parameters (weight w and bias b) of the neural network model are repeatedly updated by a known error back propagation method so that a difference between a value of output data outputted from the neural network model and an actual measurement value of the output data becomes small. As a result, the neural network model is learned, and a learned neural network model is generated. The generated learned neural network model is mounted to the ECU20 of the vehicle 1 before shipment of the vehicle 1. That is, the information (model structure, weight w, bias b, etc.) of the learned neural network model is stored in the memory 22 provided in the ECU20 or other storage device of the vehicle 1. Further, the learning unit 31 may learn the neural network model after the shipment of the vehicle 1, and the learning unit 31 may generate the learned neural network model.

When deterioration or malfunction of a vehicle component such as the actuator 11 or the sensor 12 occurs with use of the vehicle 1, replacement of the vehicle component is performed. In addition, in some cases, replacement of vehicle components may be performed in order to mount higher-performance vehicle components on the vehicle 1.

However, the neural network model mounted to the ECU20 matches the characteristics of the vehicle components before replacement. Therefore, when the characteristics of the vehicle component change due to the replacement of the vehicle component, there is a risk that the estimation accuracy of the neural network model is lowered. For example, when a vehicle component is replaced with a vehicle component of a different structure, in general, the characteristics of the vehicle component change. In addition, even when the vehicle component is replaced with a vehicle component having the same structure, there is a case where the characteristics of the vehicle component change due to individual variation.

Then, in the present embodiment, the detection unit 32 detects replacement of the vehicle component mounted on the vehicle 1. When the vehicle component related to the input data of the neural network model is replaced, the learning unit 31 creates a training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component using the replaced vehicle component, and re-learns the neural network model using the training data sets. By relearning the neural network model in accordance with the replacement of the vehicle component in this manner, it is possible to suppress a decrease in the estimation accuracy of the neural network model used in the vehicle 1 when the vehicle component is replaced.

The above control will be described in detail below with reference to the flowchart of fig. 4. Fig. 4 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the relearning process in the first embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU20 at predetermined execution intervals.

First, in step S101, the detection unit 32 determines whether the replacement flag F is 1. The replacement flag F is a flag set to 1 when the vehicle component is replaced, and the initial value of the replacement flag F is zero. In the case where it is determined in step S101 that the replacement flag F is zero, the present control routine proceeds to step S102.

In step S102, the detection unit 32 determines whether or not the vehicle component related to the input data of the neural network model has been replaced. For example, when the output value of the sensor 12 is used as input data of the neural network model, the sensor 12 corresponds to a vehicle component related to the input data of the neural network model. When the command value from the ECU20 to the actuator 11 is used as input data of the neural network model, the actuator 11 corresponds to a vehicle component related to the input data of the neural network model.

The detecting unit 32 detects replacement of the vehicle component by, for example, reading identification information (model number, serial number, manufacturing number, etc.) of the vehicle component. The detection unit 32 may detect replacement of the vehicle component by detecting an output waveform, an operating voltage, or the like of the vehicle component. The operator may input replacement of the vehicle component to an input device (HMI or the like) of the vehicle 1, and the detection unit 32 may detect replacement of the vehicle component based on the input to the input device.

In the case where it is determined in step S102 that the vehicle component is not replaced, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined in step S102 that the vehicle component is replaced, the present control routine proceeds to step S103. In step S103, the detection unit 32 sets the replacement flag F to 1.

Next, in step S104, the learning unit 31 creates a training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component. In the training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component, the output value of the replaced vehicle component, the instruction value for the replaced vehicle component, and the like are used as one of the actually measured values of the input data. The vehicle 1 is provided with a sensor 12 or the like for acquiring an actual measurement value of output data of the neural network model. Therefore, the learning unit 31 can create a training data set by combining the corresponding actual measurement values of the input data and the output data.

Next, in step S105, the learning unit 31 determines whether or not the number of training data sets corresponding to the replaced vehicle component is equal to or greater than a predetermined value. The predetermined value is predetermined and set to the number required to obtain the estimation accuracy of the required neural network model. In the case where it is determined in step S105 that the number of training data sets is smaller than the predetermined value, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined in step S105 that the number of training data sets is equal to or greater than the predetermined value, the present control routine proceeds to step S106.

In step S106, the learning unit 31 performs learning (relearning) of the neural network model using the training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component. Specifically, the learning unit 31 repeatedly updates the parameters (the weight w and the bias b) of the neural network model by a known error back propagation method, and generates a re-learned neural network model so that the difference between the value of the output data output from the neural network model and the actual measurement value of the output data becomes small.

For example, the initial values of the parameters (weight w and bias b) at the time of starting relearning are set to predetermined values. The initial value of the parameter at the time of starting relearning may be a value set before relearning, that is, a value at which the vehicle component before replacement is learned. In other words, the learning unit 31 may perform the relearning of the neural network model by updating the parameters of the neural network model set before the relearning. Accordingly, the estimation accuracy of the neural network model can be improved efficiently by relearning, and the number of training data sets required can be reduced.

Next, in step S107, the learning unit 31 applies the re-learned neural network model to the vehicle 1. In other words, the learning unit 31 updates the neural network model used in the vehicle 1. That is, the information of the neural network model stored in the memory 22 of the ECU20 or other storage device is rewritten. By using the neural network model after re-learning in the vehicle 1, the value of the output data corresponding to the input data of the predetermined value can be estimated without detecting the actual value of the output data by the sensor 12 or the like.

Next, in step S108, the learning unit 31 sets the replacement flag F to zero. After step S108, the present control routine ends.

Further, the characteristics of the vehicle component may vary greatly when the vehicle component is replaced with a vehicle component of a different structure. Therefore, the learning unit 31 may perform the re-learning of the neural network model by using the training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component only when the vehicle component related to the input data of the neural network model is replaced with a vehicle component having a different structure. This can effectively suppress a decrease in the estimation accuracy of the neural network model, and reduce the amount of power consumption for relearning. In this case, in step S102, the detection unit 32 determines whether or not the vehicle component related to the input data of the neural network model is replaced with a vehicle component of a different configuration.

< Second embodiment >

The configuration and control of the machine learning device according to the second embodiment are basically the same as those of the machine learning device according to the first embodiment except for the points described below. Therefore, the second embodiment of the present invention will be described below mainly with respect to the portions different from the first embodiment.

Fig. 5 is a schematic configuration diagram of a client server system 10 to which the machine learning device according to the second embodiment of the present invention is applied. The client server system 10 includes the vehicle 1' and the server 4. The server 4 is capable of communicating with a plurality of vehicles including the vehicle 1'.

As shown in fig. 5, the server 4 is provided outside the vehicle 1', and includes a communication interface 41, a storage device 42, a memory 43, and a processor 44. The server 4 may further include an input device such as a keyboard and a mouse, an output device such as a display, and the like. The server 4 may be constituted by a plurality of computers.

The communication interface 41 is capable of communicating with the vehicle 1 'and enables the server 4 to communicate with the vehicle 1'. Specifically, the communication interface 41 has an interface circuit for connecting the server 4 to the communication network 5. The server 4 communicates with the vehicle 1' via the communication interface 41, the communication network 5, and the wireless base station 6. The communication interface 41 is an example of a communication apparatus.

The storage device 42 has, for example, a Hard Disk Drive (HDD), a Solid State Drive (SSD), an optical recording medium, and the like. The storage device 42 stores various data, such as computer programs or the like for the processor 44 to perform various processes.

The memory 43 has, for example, a semiconductor memory such as a Random Access Memory (RAM). The memory 43 stores, for example, various data and the like used when various processes are executed by the processor 44.

The communication interface 41, the storage device 42, and the memory 43 are connected to the processor 44 via signal lines. The processor 44 has one or more CPUs and peripheral circuits thereof, and performs various processes. The processor 44 may further include an arithmetic circuit such as a logic arithmetic unit or a numerical arithmetic unit. Processor 44 is an example of a control device.

Fig. 6 is a diagram schematically showing a part of the structure of the vehicle 1' of fig. 5. As shown in fig. 6, the vehicle 1' has a communication module 13 on the basis of the actuator 11, the sensor 12, and the ECU 20. The actuator 11, the sensor 12, and the communication module 13 are communicably connected to the ECU20 via an in-vehicle network conforming to the standard CAN (Controller Area Network) or the like.

The communication module 13 is a device that enables communication between the vehicle 1 'and the outside of the vehicle 1'. The communication module 13 is, for example, a data communication module (DCM (Data communication module)) capable of communicating with the communication network 5 via the radio base station 6. Further, as the communication module 13, a portable terminal (for example, a smart phone, a tablet terminal, a WiFi router, or the like) may be used. The communication module 13 is an example of a communication apparatus.

In the second embodiment, the ECU20 functions as a part of the machine learning device. Fig. 7 is a functional block diagram of the ECU20 of fig. 6. The ECU20 has a detection portion 32 and an update portion 33. The detection section 32 and the update section 33 are functional blocks realized by the processor 23 of the ECU20 executing programs stored in the memory 22 of the ECU 20.

The detection unit 32 detects replacement of a vehicle component mounted on the vehicle 1, as in the first embodiment. The updating unit 33 updates the neural network model used in the vehicle 1'.

In the second embodiment, learning of the neural network model used in the vehicle 1 'is performed in the server 4, and the learned neural network model is transmitted from the server 4 to the vehicle 1'. That is, the processor 44 of the server 4 functions as a learning unit that learns the neural network model used in the vehicle 1'.

When the vehicle component related to the input data of the neural network model is replaced, the processor 44 performs relearning of the neural network model using the training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component, and transmits the relearned neural network model to the vehicle 1'. The updating unit 33 of the vehicle 1 'applies the relearned neural network model to the vehicle 1' when receiving the relearned neural network model from the server 4. By relearning the neural network model in accordance with the replacement of the vehicle component in this manner, it is possible to suppress a decrease in the estimation accuracy of the neural network model used in the vehicle 1' when the vehicle component is replaced.

The above control will be described in detail below with reference to flowcharts of fig. 8 and 9. Fig. 8 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the model update process in the second embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU20 of the vehicle 1' at predetermined execution intervals.

First, in step S201, the detection unit 32 determines whether the replacement flag F is 1. The replacement flag F is a flag set to 1 when the vehicle component is replaced, and the initial value of the replacement flag F is zero. In the case where it is determined in step S201 that the replacement flag F is zero, the present control routine proceeds to step S202.

In step S202, the detection unit 32 determines whether or not the vehicle component related to the input data of the neural network model has been replaced, as in step S102 of fig. 4. In the case where it is determined that the replacement of the vehicle component has not been performed, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, in the case where it is determined that the replacement of the vehicle component is performed, the present control routine proceeds to step S203.

In step S203, the detection unit 32 sets the replacement flag F to 1. After step S203, the present control routine advances to step S204. On the other hand, in the case where it is determined in step S201 that the replacement flag F is 1, the present control routine proceeds to step S204 by skipping steps S202 and S203.

In step S204, the updating unit 33 creates a training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component. In the training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component, the output value of the replaced vehicle component, the instruction value for the replaced vehicle component, and the like are used as one of the actually measured values of the input data. The vehicle 1' is provided with a sensor 12 or the like for capturing an actual measurement value of output data of the neural network model. Therefore, the updating unit 33 can create a training data set by combining the corresponding actual measurement values of the input data and the output data.

Next, in step S205, the updating unit 33 transmits the training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component to the server 4.

Next, in step S206, the updating unit 33 determines whether or not the re-learned neural network model is received from the server 4. If it is determined that the neural network model has not been re-learned for the purpose of not being received, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, in the case where it is determined that the neural network model has been re-learned for reception, the present control routine proceeds to step S207.

In step S207, the updating section 33 applies the relearned neural network model to the vehicle 1'. In other words, the updating unit 33 updates the neural network model used in the vehicle 1'. That is, the information of the neural network model stored in the memory 22 of the ECU20 or other storage device is rewritten.

Next, in step S208, the updating unit 33 resets the replacement flag F to zero. After step S109, the present control routine ends.

Fig. 9 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the relearning process in the second embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the processor 44 of the server 4 at predetermined execution intervals.

First, in step S301, the processor 44 determines whether a training data set corresponding to a replaced vehicle component is received from the vehicle 1'. In the case where it is determined that the training data set is not received, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, in the case where it is determined that the training data set is received, the present control routine proceeds to step S302.

In step S302, the processor 44 determines whether the number of training data sets corresponding to the replaced vehicle component is a predetermined value or more. The predetermined value is predetermined and set to the number required to obtain the estimation accuracy of the required neural network model. In the case where it is determined in step S302 that the number of training data sets is smaller than the predetermined value, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, in the case where it is determined in step S302 that the number of training data sets is equal to or greater than the predetermined value, the present control routine proceeds to step S303.

In step S303, the processor 44 performs learning (relearning) of the neural network model using the training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component. Specifically, the processor 44 repeatedly updates the parameters (the weight w and the bias b) of the neural network model by a known error back propagation method, and generates a re-learned neural network model so that the difference between the value of the output data outputted from the neural network model and the actual measurement value of the output data becomes small.

For example, the initial values of the parameters (weight w and bias b) at the time of starting relearning are set to predetermined values. The initial value of the parameter at the time of starting relearning may be a value set before relearning, that is, a value at which the vehicle component before replacement is learned. In other words, the processor 44 may perform the relearning of the neural network model by updating the parameters of the neural network model set before the relearning. Accordingly, the estimation accuracy of the neural network model can be improved efficiently by relearning, and the number of training data sets required can be reduced.

Next, in step S304, the processor 44 transmits the relearned neural network model to the vehicle 1'. After step S304, the present control routine ends.

Further, the training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component may be transmitted from a vehicle other than the vehicle 1' to the server 4. The training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component may be created in the server 4 using an engine mount or the like.

In addition, as described above, the characteristics of the vehicle component may vary greatly when the vehicle component is replaced with a vehicle component of a different structure. Therefore, the processor 44 may perform the re-learning of the neural network model by using the training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component only when the vehicle component related to the input data of the neural network model is replaced with a vehicle component having a different structure. This can effectively suppress a decrease in the estimation accuracy of the neural network model, and reduce the amount of power consumption for relearning. In this case, in step S202, the detection unit 32 determines whether or not the vehicle component related to the input data of the neural network model is replaced with a vehicle component of a different configuration.

While the preferred embodiments of the present invention have been described above, the present invention is not limited to these embodiments, and various modifications and changes can be made within the scope of the claims. For example, the machine learning model used in the vehicle 1,1' may be a machine learning model other than a neural network such as a random forest, a k-nearest neighbor method, or a support vector machine.
